hero.lead: A traiteur in Brussels for private hosts and companies. Seasonal plates, cooked each morning and delivered ready to serve.

intro.headline: A traiteur in Brussels for people who care how it tastes — and how it looks.
intro.body: We cook for private hosts and companies across the city. Seasonal plates, salads and cold-pressed juices, prepared each morning and delivered ready to serve. We run events end to end, and keep a coffee desk open for anyone passing by.

kitchen.label: The kitchen
kitchen.title: Cooked the morning it is eaten.
kitchen.body: We start before dawn, when the city is still quiet. Plates, salads and cold-pressed juices are made from scratch that same morning — seasonal produce, sauces reduced overnight, dressings mixed at the last minute. Nothing reheated, nothing left over from the day before.

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.title: Prepared at dawn, served by lunch.
delivery.body: We pack and send across Brussels in the early hours, so lunch arrives as the kitchen intended. Insulated boxes, portions already set, garnishes kept separate — ready to unwrap and serve at your desk, in a meeting room, or at home before your guests walk in.

hosting.label: The table
hosting.title: A table set for the room.
hosting.body: Seasonal menus, quiet service, timing held end to end — for hosts who want the table to say something about them.

statement.headline: Food that holds the table, not just the plate — cooked that morning, ready to serve.
body: Every collection leaves the same kitchen in Brussels — seasonal plates, salads, pastries and cold-pressed juices, cooked that morning from raw ingredients. Nothing reheated, nothing bought in finished: what goes out is what we would plate at the pass.
Pick what suits the desk, the house or the room — lunch for ten, drinks for thirty, a seated dinner. We handle the timing, the delivery and what needs to be on the table on time, ready to serve.

items.title: Delivery
items.body: Plates, salads and juices prepared each morning and delivered ready to serve — to a desk, a boardroom or a kitchen table.

items.title: Events
items.body: From a twenty-person launch to a seated dinner. We handle the menu, the service and everything that has to happen before the doors open.

items.title: Coffee
items.body: A coffee desk for anyone passing by, and the same pastries and juices we send out to our clients.

whyUs.label: Why choose us
whyUs.headline: Good food is the easy part. This is the rest of it.

reasons.title: One number to call
reasons.body: The person who answers writes the menu, and is still the person answering the week of the delivery. Nothing is subcontracted, so nothing is lost between two companies.

reasons.title: Quoted per head, all in
reasons.body: Delivery, service, equipment and collection are in the figure we send you. No line items appearing three days before the event.

reasons.title: Diets planned, not patched
reasons.body: Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free versions of the same dish, labelled and boxed separately. Nobody is handed a plate of side dishes.

reasons.title: A window we keep
reasons.body: Brussels traffic is a known quantity, so we leave early and we call before you have to. If something moves, you hear it at six in the morning, not at noon.

hero.title: About
hero.lead: Moment is a traiteur in Brussels. We cook for private hosts and for companies who want the food to say something about them.

intro.headline: We cook for whoever has to feed the room.
body: Moment is a traiteur and catering kitchen in Brussels. Every morning we cook seasonal plates, salads, pastries and cold-pressed juices, then send them out across the city — to offices in the European quarter, to studios in Saint-Gilles, to kitchen tables in between.

Some weeks that is forty lunches before ten in the morning. Some weeks it is a seated dinner for thirty, a launch for two hundred, or a coffee desk open until the room empties. The logistics change. The kitchen behind them does not.

statement.headline: The table is the first place people meet you.

items.title: Cooked that morning
items.body: Plates, salads and cold-pressed juices leave our kitchen the day they are eaten — nothing reheated, nothing from the day before.

items.title: Delivered ready to plate
items.body: Portions already set, garnishes kept separate, insulated boxes. You unwrap, arrange and serve.

items.title: Built for the room
items.body: A desk lunch, a launch, a seated dinner — the menu follows the covers and the pace of your day.

story.label: Our story
story.title: It began with one table too many.
story.body: Moment started in a rented kitchen off the Chaussée d'Ixelles, cooking Friday lunch for a design studio that had run out of decent options. Word travelled the way it does here — one office told another, then someone's launch, then someone's wedding. We still cook to order, still cap the covers at what we can plate properly, and still send out nothing we would not happily eat standing at the pass.

items.title: Seasonal, or not at all
items.body: The menu follows the market rather than the other way round. Asparagus in May, tomatoes when they actually taste of something, chicory and game through the winter. If it is not good this week, it is not on the list this week.

items.title: Cooked, never assembled
items.body: Stocks reduced overnight, dressings mixed at the last minute, pastry laminated by hand. Everything leaves our own kitchen in Brussels, made from raw ingredients that same morning — nothing reheated, nothing bought in finished.

items.title: Delivered ready to serve
items.body: Insulated boxes, portions already set, garnishes kept separate. You unwrap it, arrange it and serve it. No kitchen needed at your end, and nothing that has to be plated by someone who would rather be hosting.

items.title: One kitchen, one standard
items.body: The same food goes to a two-person desk lunch and a two-hundred-guest reception. Scale changes the number of hands and the hour we start, not the recipe or what we are willing to send out.

sourcing.label: Sourcing
sourcing.title: We buy short, and we buy close.
sourcing.body: Vegetables from Flemish and Walloon market gardens, bread from a bakery two streets away, fish only when the North Sea sends something worth serving. We order small and often rather than large and once, which is why the menu moves through the year — and why so little is thrown away. What does not go out, the team eats.
